assumptions: The NL states that there are twelve finite states but does not provide their exact original names or all exact branch formulas; this model names twelve dispatch-condition states from the described operating cases.

The phrase 'SoC is suitable' and 'low-SoC branches' is represented by a declared parameter SoC_low_limit rather than an invented fixed threshold, while the explicit 0.95 threshold is modeled directly.

The model is a guard-driven condition-classification abstraction: global forced guard transitions dynamically select the active dispatch state from current inputs rather than relying on separate event memory.

Per-generator requested power allocation is abstracted into aggregate requested_generator_power plus cut-in/cut-out flags, because the NL only requires returned requested generator power and cut commands, not exact unit-level sharing.
DG3 is represented through eng3_Pmax because the NL cites eng3_Pmax as an engine capacity bound; DG1 and DG2 are modeled as last-priority diesel branches from the explicit DG1/DG2 priority statement.

grounding_seeds.evidence_text: When Ppv + Pw covers PL, the EMS serves all ship demand from RES and charges batteries while SoC is below 0.95.
When Ppv + Pw covers PL... treats residual renewable power as spare once SoC is at least 0.95.
When PL = 0, RES production is sent to battery charging... according to SoC thresholds.
When PL = 0, RES production is sent... to spare power according to SoC thresholds.
When Ppv + Pw is below PL, dispatch follows the stated priority: RES first, batteries when SoC is suitable.
Dispatch follows the stated priority... LNG before diesel units.
Low-SoC branches add explicit charging margins, including Pgmax/5 in an LNG-covered case.
The FSM reads... engine capacity bounds such as eng3_Pmax; dispatch uses LNG before diesel units.

accepted_edit_intent: Replace SoC_low_limit guard reads with literal 0.20
decisions.rationale: SoC_low_limit is a fixed modeling threshold, not an NL-described time-varying input. The smallest safe repair is to inline its initialized value 0.20 in the guards and remove the unwritten variable declaration, as suggested by the diagnostic.
battery_Pmax is a capacity/input bound used to classify demand coverage. The NL does not provide runtime update semantics for it, and adding writes would invent plant dynamics.
Plngmax is a generator capacity/input bound. The NL requires dispatch against capacity bounds but does not define an internal update, so writing it would be ungrounded.
Pd2max is a diesel-generator capacity/input bound. It should remain externally supplied/read-only in this dispatch classifier because no NL update rule is provided.
The BatteryAssist guard is intentionally driven by external/time-varying inputs PL, Ppv, Pw, SoC and capacity battery_Pmax. Adding dummy writes would violate the forbidden edits.
The LNGDispatch guard is an NL-grounded condition over demand, renewable generation, SoC, battery capacity and LNG capacity. These are external inputs/capacity bounds, not internal FSM state updates.
The LNGChargeMargin guard is NL-grounded and depends on demand, renewables, SoC, Pgmax and LNG capacity. No safe internal write is specified by the NL.
The LNGDG3Dispatch guard reads external demand/resource values and capacity bounds including eng3_Pmax. It should not be altered solely to silence never-change diagnostics.

diff_summary.summary: Removed the SoC_low_limit declaration and replaced all SoC_low_limit guard references with the literal threshold 0.20. No states, dispatch actions, capacity variables, output variables, or required guards were deleted.

repair_rationale: Accepted only the safe constant-threshold repair: SoC_low_limit had no independent NL-required variable identity and was initialized to 0.20, so inlining preserves behavior while removing an unwritten-read warning.

Preserved all twelve required finite states and all required output actions, cut-in/cut-out commands, and dispatch guards including RES cover, zero-load, battery assist, LNG, DG3, DG1/DG2 last-priority, and extreme overload branches.

Rejected/waived capacity/input write requests for battery_Pmax, Plngmax, Pd2max and guard-never-change warnings because PL, Ppv, Pw, SoC and capacity bounds are NL-described external inputs or capacity parameters. Adding artificial writes would violate the repair instruction not to invent plant/environment dynamics.
The candidate remains a guard-driven condition-classification FSM using forced guard transitions to dynamically select dispatch states from current external inputs.

evidence.summary: The only accepted edit removes the non-NL variable SoC_low_limit and replaces its guard reads with the initialized literal 0.20. This preserves the same low-SoC threshold behavior while resolving that unwritten-read request without deleting any NL-required state, output, guard, or dispatch branch.

The candidate DSL preserves all twelve required finite states: RESCoversCharge, RESCoversSpare, ZeroLoadCharge, ZeroLoadSpare, BatteryAssist, LNGDispatch, LNGChargeMargin, LNGDG3Dispatch, LNGDG3ChargeMargin, AddDG1LastPriority, AddDG2LastPriority, and ExtremeOverloadBatteryLack.

The candidate continues to implement the NL dispatch priorities and outputs: RES coverage charges or creates spare based on SoC 0.95; zero-load sends RES to battery or spare; deficit cases use battery, LNG, DG3, DG1/DG2 last-priority branches; low-SoC charging margins Pgmax/5 and Pd1max/10 remain; extreme overload activates all thermal units and covers the lack by battery discharge with illegal_overload marked.

The SL-9 decisions correctly waived the remaining non-hard design warnings for battery_Pmax, Plngmax, Pd2max, and guard-never-change diagnostics because the NL describes PL, Ppv, Pw, SoC, and capacity bounds as read inputs/parameters for dispatch classification, not internal FSM variables with specified update equations.

The DSL diff is narrow and non-regressive: it only deletes def float SoC_low_limit and substitutes 0.20 in guards; no required preserve element, cut-in/cut-out command, capacity variable used by dispatch, output action, or required guard was removed.

local_override_rationale: Local SD-10 rejects with reason design_target_unresolved because warnings remain for unwritten read variables such as battery_Pmax, Plngmax, and Pd2max, and guard variables that never change. These warnings are conservative for a guard-driven condition-classification FSM whose guards are intentionally driven by externally supplied demand, renewable generation, SoC, and capacity bounds. The NL explicitly says the FSM reads PL, Ppv, Pw, SoC, and capacity bounds and dynamically selects states as resources and demands vary; it does not require or define internal writes for those inputs.

Adding action/effect writes to battery_Pmax, Plngmax, Pd2max, PL, Ppv, Pw, or SoC solely to satisfy the local warnings would invent plant/environment dynamics and violate the request batch forbidden edit: do not invent internal plant/environment dynamics merely to make external input variables appear written. Simplifying or removing the affected guards would reduce NL fidelity because those guards encode the required capacity/demand/SoC dispatch branches.

The one variable that was safely repairable, SoC_low_limit, was not an NL-required input or output and had only a fixed modeling-threshold role. Inlining its initialized value 0.20 resolves that actionable warning while preserving behavior. The remaining local unresolved items are intentionally waived non-hard warnings, not evidence of scenario regression or NL-fidelity regression.

Local evidence reports regression_detected=false and drift_risk=none, with no actionable scenario repair items. Therefore, despite target_resolved=false in the local deterministic review, the NL requirements plus FixLog ledger justify accepting the candidate for the next full top-down revalidation pass.

This preserves the same low-SoC threshold behavior while resolving that unwritten-read request without deleting any NL-required state, output, guard, or dispatch branch.

The candidate DSL preserves all twelve required finite states: RESCoversCharge, RESCoversSpare, ZeroLoadCharge, ZeroLoadSpare, BatteryAssist, LNGDispatch, LNGChargeMargin, LNGDG3Dispatch, LNGDG3ChargeMargin, AddDG1LastPriority, AddDG2LastPriority, and ExtremeOverloadBatteryLack.

The candidate continues to implement the NL dispatch priorities and outputs: RES coverage charges or creates spare based on SoC 0.95; zero-load sends RES to battery or spare; deficit cases use battery, LNG, DG3, DG1/DG2 last-priority branches; low-SoC charging margins Pgmax/5 and Pd1max/10 remain; extreme overload activates all thermal units and covers the lack by battery discharge with illegal_overload marked.

The SL-9 decisions correctly waived the remaining non-hard design warnings for battery_Pmax, Plngmax, Pd2max, and guard-never-change diagnostics because the NL describes PL, Ppv, Pw, SoC, and capacity bounds as read inputs/parameters for dispatch classification, not internal FSM variables with specified update equations.

The DSL diff is narrow and non-regressive: it only deletes def float SoC_low_limit and substitutes 0.20 in guards; no required preserve element, cut-in/cut-out command, capacity variable used by dispatch, output action, or required guard was removed.

local_override_rationale: Local SD-10 rejects with reason design_target_unresolved because warnings remain for unwritten read variables such as battery_Pmax, Plngmax, and Pd2max, and guard variables that never change. These warnings are conservative for a guard-driven condition-classification FSM whose guards are intentionally driven by externally supplied demand, renewable generation, SoC, and capacity bounds. The NL explicitly says the FSM reads PL, Ppv, Pw, SoC, and capacity bounds and dynamically selects states as resources and demands vary; it does not require or define internal writes for those inputs.

Adding action/effect writes to battery_Pmax, Plngmax, Pd2max, PL, Ppv, Pw, or SoC solely to satisfy the local warnings would invent plant/environment dynamics and violate the request batch forbidden edit: do not invent internal plant/environment dynamics merely to make external input variables appear written. Simplifying or removing the affected guards would reduce NL fidelity because those guards encode the required capacity/demand/SoC dispatch branches.

The one variable that was safely repairable, SoC_low_limit, was not an NL-required input or output and had only a fixed modeling-threshold role. Inlining its initialized value 0.20 resolves that actionable warning while preserving behavior. The remaining local unresolved items are intentionally waived non-hard warnings, not evidence of scenario regression or NL-fidelity regression.

Local evidence reports regression_detected=false and drift_risk=none, with no actionable scenario repair items. Therefore, despite target_resolved=false in the local deterministic review, the NL requirements plus FixLog ledger justify accepting the candidate for the next full top-down revalidation pass.

decisions.rationale: SoC_low_limit is a fixed modeling threshold, not an NL-described time-varying input. The smallest safe repair is to inline its initialized value 0.20 in the guards and remove the unwritten variable declaration, as suggested by the diagnostic.
battery_Pmax is a capacity/input bound used to classify demand coverage. The NL does not provide runtime update semantics for it, and adding writes would invent plant dynamics.
Plngmax is a generator capacity/input bound. The NL requires dispatch against capacity bounds but does not define an internal update, so writing it would be ungrounded.
Pd2max is a diesel-generator capacity/input bound. It should remain externally supplied/read-only in this dispatch classifier because no NL update rule is provided.
The BatteryAssist guard is intentionally driven by external/time-varying inputs PL, Ppv, Pw, SoC and capacity battery_Pmax. Adding dummy writes would violate the forbidden edits.
The LNGDispatch guard is an NL-grounded condition over demand, renewable generation, SoC, battery capacity and LNG capacity. These are external inputs/capacity bounds, not internal FSM state updates.
The LNGChargeMargin guard is NL-grounded and depends on demand, renewables, SoC, Pgmax and LNG capacity. No safe internal write is specified by the NL.
The LNGDG3Dispatch guard reads external demand/resource values and capacity bounds including eng3_Pmax. It should not be altered solely to silence never-change diagnostics.
The LNGDG3ChargeMargin guard is a required low-SoC/capacity branch. Its variables are external inputs or capacity parameters, and the NL gives no update equations.
The AddDG1LastPriority guard implements the required last-priority DG1 branch over demand and capacity inputs. Simplifying or adding writes would reduce NL fidelity.

diff_summary.summary: Removed the SoC_low_limit declaration and replaced all SoC_low_limit guard references with the literal threshold 0.20. No states, dispatch actions, capacity variables, output variables, or required guards were deleted.

repair_rationale: Accepted only the safe constant-threshold repair: SoC_low_limit had no independent NL-required variable identity and was initialized to 0.20, so inlining preserves behavior while removing an unwritten-read warning.

Preserved all twelve required finite states and all required output actions, cut-in/cut-out commands, and dispatch guards including RES cover, zero-load, battery assist, LNG, DG3, DG1/DG2 last-priority, and extreme overload branches.

Rejected/waived capacity/input write requests for battery_Pmax, Plngmax, Pd2max and guard-never-change warnings because PL, Ppv, Pw, SoC and capacity bounds are NL-described external inputs or capacity parameters. Adding artificial writes would violate the repair instruction not to invent plant/environment dynamics.
The candidate remains a guard-driven condition-classification FSM using forced guard transitions to dynamically select dispatch states from current external inputs.

decisions.rationale: battery_Pmax is an NL-grounded capacity/input bound used to classify whether battery assist can cover the residual demand. The NL says the FSM reads capacity bounds and does not define an internal update rule. Adding a write would invent plant dynamics, and this same issue was already waived in FixLog with no new evidence.

Plngmax is an externally supplied LNG capacity bound. It is intentionally read by dispatch guards and actions; the NL provides no meaningful FSM-side update. The prior FixLog already waived this warning, and the new batch provides no new evidence requiring a DSL change.

Pd2max is an externally supplied diesel-generator capacity bound used in the DG2 last-priority and extreme-overload branches. Writing it internally would be ungrounded. This request repeats a previously waived issue without new evidence.

The BatteryAssist guard is intentionally controlled by external/time-varying inputs PL, Ppv, Pw, SoC and the capacity bound battery_Pmax. The NL explicitly says the FSM reads these values as inputs. Adding dummy writes or simplifying the guard would reduce NL fidelity, and the same warning was previously waived.

The LNGDispatch guard implements the NL dispatch condition over residual demand, battery capacity, SoC, and LNG capacity. All guard variables are external inputs or capacity parameters with no NL update semantics. Prior SL-10 override treated this as an audit-only local objection.

The LNGChargeMargin guard is required for the low-SoC branch with Pgmax/5 charging margin. Its variables are NL-grounded demand/resource/capacity inputs. No safe internal write exists, and changing the guard would risk deleting a required branch.

The LNGDG3Dispatch guard uses residual demand and engine/LNG capacity bounds including eng3_Pmax, matching the NL requirement to use capacity bounds for dispatch. The guard-never-change warning is conservative for this input-classification FSM and was previously waived.

The LNGDG3ChargeMargin guard is an NL-required low-SoC diesel-generator charging-margin branch using Pd1max/10 and capacity bounds. Adding writes to external inputs would invent dynamics, while simplifying the guard would reduce coverage.

decisions.rationale: battery_Pmax is an NL-grounded capacity/input bound used to classify whether battery assist can cover the residual demand. The NL says the FSM reads capacity bounds and does not define an internal update rule. Adding a write would invent plant dynamics, and this same issue was already waived in FixLog with no new evidence.

Plngmax is an externally supplied LNG capacity bound. It is intentionally read by dispatch guards and actions; the NL provides no meaningful FSM-side update. The prior FixLog already waived this warning, and the new batch provides no new evidence requiring a DSL change.

Pd2max is an externally supplied diesel-generator capacity bound used in the DG2 last-priority and extreme-overload branches. Writing it internally would be ungrounded. This request repeats a previously waived issue without new evidence.

The BatteryAssist guard is intentionally controlled by external/time-varying inputs PL, Ppv, Pw, SoC and the capacity bound battery_Pmax. The NL explicitly says the FSM reads these values as inputs. Adding dummy writes or simplifying the guard would reduce NL fidelity, and the same warning was previously waived.

The LNGDispatch guard implements the NL dispatch condition over residual demand, battery capacity, SoC, and LNG capacity. All guard variables are external inputs or capacity parameters with no NL update semantics. Prior SL-10 override treated this as an audit-only local objection.

The LNGChargeMargin guard is required for the low-SoC branch with Pgmax/5 charging margin. Its variables are NL-grounded demand/resource/capacity inputs. No safe internal write exists, and changing the guard would risk deleting a required branch.

The LNGDG3Dispatch guard uses residual demand and engine/LNG capacity bounds including eng3_Pmax, matching the NL requirement to use capacity bounds for dispatch. The guard-never-change warning is conservative for this input-classification FSM and was previously waived.

The LNGDG3ChargeMargin guard is an NL-required low-SoC diesel-generator charging-margin branch using Pd1max/10 and capacity bounds. Adding writes to external inputs would invent dynamics, while simplifying the guard would reduce coverage.

The AddDG1LastPriority guard implements the required last-priority DG1 dispatch branch. Its variables are demand, renewable contributions, and capacity bounds read from the environment/system configuration. No NL-grounded repair exists beyond waiver.

The AddDG2LastPriority guard implements the required last-priority DG2 branch and depends on externally supplied capacity bounds including Pd2max. A dummy write or constant rewrite is forbidden and would degrade the model.

The ExtremeOverloadBatteryLack guard is required by the overload requirement: when demand exceeds all RES and thermal resources, all thermal units are activated and the lack is covered by battery discharge. Its guard variables are external inputs/capacity bounds, and the prior ledger already waived the warning.

The RESCoversSpare-to-BatteryAssist guard is another instance of the same NL-grounded dynamic dispatch classification over external demand/resource/SoC/capacity inputs. No new hard evidence or scenario regression reopens the prior waiver.

variable_role_summary.policy: Advisory only. Do not invent writes for external_input_candidate variables unless NL explicitly gives update semantics; add meaningful NL-grounded writes only for internal state variables.
variable_role_summary.source: SD-4 diagnostic refs and generic NL external-input rationale

decisions.rationale: battery_Pmax is an NL-grounded capacity/input bound used to classify whether battery assist can cover the residual demand. The NL says the FSM reads capacity bounds and does not define an internal update rule. Adding a write would invent plant dynamics, and this same issue was already waived in FixLog with no new evidence.

Plngmax is an externally supplied LNG capacity bound. It is intentionally read by dispatch guards and actions; the NL provides no meaningful FSM-side update. The prior FixLog already waived this warning, and the new batch provides no new evidence requiring a DSL change.

Pd2max is an externally supplied diesel-generator capacity bound used in the DG2 last-priority and extreme-overload branches. Writing it internally would be ungrounded. This request repeats a previously waived issue without new evidence.

The BatteryAssist guard is intentionally controlled by external/time-varying inputs PL, Ppv, Pw, SoC and the capacity bound battery_Pmax. The NL explicitly says the FSM reads these values as inputs. Adding dummy writes or simplifying the guard would reduce NL fidelity, and the same warning was previously waived.

The LNGDispatch guard implements the NL dispatch condition over residual demand, battery capacity, SoC, and LNG capacity. All guard variables are external inputs or capacity parameters with no NL update semantics. Prior SL-10 override treated this as an audit-only local objection.

The LNGChargeMargin guard is required for the low-SoC branch with Pgmax/5 charging margin. Its variables are NL-grounded demand/resource/capacity inputs. No safe internal write exists, and changing the guard would risk deleting a required branch.

The LNGDG3Dispatch guard uses residual demand and engine/LNG capacity bounds including eng3_Pmax, matching the NL requirement to use capacity bounds for dispatch. The guard-never-change warning is conservative for this input-classification FSM and was previously waived.

The LNGDG3ChargeMargin guard is an NL-required low-SoC diesel-generator charging-margin branch using Pd1max/10 and capacity bounds. Adding writes to external inputs would invent dynamics, while simplifying the guard would reduce coverage.

The AddDG1LastPriority guard implements the required last-priority DG1 dispatch branch. Its variables are demand, renewable contributions, and capacity bounds read from the environment/system configuration. No NL-grounded repair exists beyond waiver.

The AddDG2LastPriority guard implements the required last-priority DG2 branch and depends on externally supplied capacity bounds including Pd2max. A dummy write or constant rewrite is forbidden and would degrade the model.

diff_summary.summary: No DSL edit produced. All twelve requests are waived/rejected as repeated external-input/capacity-bound warnings with no new actionable evidence.

repair_rationale: All current requests repeat design warnings already rejected/waived in the FixLog and explicitly overridden by SL-10 as audit-only local objections.

The variables battery_Pmax, Plngmax, Pd2max, PL, Ppv, Pw, SoC, Pgmax, eng3_Pmax, and Pd1max are NL-grounded external inputs or capacity bounds used by a guard-driven dispatch classifier. The NL says the FSM reads these values; it does not define internal update equations.

The smallest safe action is therefore no DSL edit. Adding writes would violate the forbidden edit against inventing plant/environment dynamics, while simplifying/removing guards would break required states and dispatch branches.
Because every current request is rejected/waived and no request is accepted, the SL-9 contract requires candidate_dsl to remain empty rather than returning an unchanged DSL candidate.

scenario_results.name: res_covers_spare_at_soc_threshold

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start: in a later low-SoC diesel-generator case, the Pd1max/10 charging margin should be added while using LNG and DG3.
scenario_results.name: lng_dg3_charge_margin_pd1_margin

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start: when the deficit exceeds LNG plus DG3 but exactly fits after adding DG1, DG1 is cut in and DG2 remains cut out.

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start: when the deficit exceeds LNG plus DG3 plus DG1 but exactly fits after adding DG2, both DG1 and DG2 are cut in as last-priority units.
scenario_results.name: add_dg2_last_priority_boundary

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start: for demand exceeding all RES and thermal resources, all thermal units are activated and the remaining lack is covered by battery discharge in the illegal overload state.
scenario_results.name: extreme_overload_all_thermal_and_battery_lack

decisions.rationale: The failing scenario default_init_zero_load_charge initializes PL=0.0, Ppv=10.0, Pw=5.0, SoC=0.5 and expects the first default-init cycle to classify into LNGShipEMS.ZeroLoadCharge with cut_in_load=0 and cut_out_load=1. evidence.summary: The hard simulation request fixreq-2-sd6-0-99efbfa439 is substantively resolved by the candidate DSL. The failing scenario default_init_zero_load_charge initialized PL=0.0, Ppv=10.0, Pw=5.0, SoC=0.5 and expected LNGShipEMS.ZeroLoadCharge with requested_generator_power=0.0, battery_discharge_power=0.0, battery_charging_power=15.0, spare_power=0.0, cut_in_load=0, cut_out_load=1, cut_in_LNG=0, and cut_out_LNG=1. The old DSL entered RESCoversCharge because the root initial transition was hardwired to RESCoversCharge, producing the right charging power but wrong load cut commands. The candidate replaces that fixed initial target with InitialDispatchSelect and routes PL == 0 && SoC < 0.95 to ZeroLoadCharge, whose existing enter action sets the expected outputs.

The DSL diff is targeted: [*] -> RESCoversCharge is changed to [*] -> InitialDispatchSelect, a pseudo selector is added, and twelve guarded outgoing selector transitions mirror the existing dispatch classification guards. No NL-required output variables, capacity/input variables, cut-in/cut-out commands, state actions, forced dynamic transitions, or dispatch states are removed.

The NL requires twelve finite dispatch states selected by logical conditions over demand, renewable generation, capacity, and SoC. The candidate preserves all twelve required finite states: RESCoversCharge, RESCoversSpare, ZeroLoadCharge, ZeroLoadSpare, BatteryAssist, LNGDispatch, LNGChargeMargin, LNGDG3Dispatch, LNGDG3ChargeMargin, AddDG1LastPriority, AddDG2LastPriority, and ExtremeOverloadBatteryLack. The added InitialDispatchSelect is a pseudo routing state rather than a replacement for or deletion of any required finite state.

The candidate preserves NL dispatch fidelity: zero-load branches route RES to charging or spare by SoC threshold; RES-covered nonzero load branches charge or spare by SoC 0.95; deficit branches maintain RES-first, battery-when-suitable, LNG-before-diesel, DG1/DG2-last-priority behavior; low-SoC charging margins Pgmax/5 and Pd1max/10 remain; and the extreme overload branch still activates all thermal units, discharges the battery lack, and marks illegal_overload.

The complete FixLog shows that earlier local design warnings about unwritten external inputs/capacity bounds and guard variables that never change were deliberately waived and then overridden by SL-10 because the NL describes PL, Ppv, Pw, SoC, battery_Pmax, Plngmax, Pgmax, Pd1max, Pd2max, and eng3_Pmax as read inputs or capacity bounds, not internally updated plant dynamics. The current accepted SL-9 edit does not reopen those waived issues by adding dummy writes or simplifying required guards.

Local deterministic evidence reports no scenario regression and no semantic runtime error, but rejects on new InitialDispatchSelect guard-never-change diagnostics and forced_transition_count_drift. Those are structural/design objections arising from the intentional pseudo selector, not evidence that the hard simulation scenario remains behaviorally wrong.

local_override_rationale: Local SD-10 reports target_resolved=false with reason new_blocking_design_diagnostic because the new InitialDispatchSelect outgoing guards read PL, Ppv, Pw, SoC, battery_Pmax, Plngmax, Pgmax, Pd1max, Pd2max, and eng3_Pmax, which are not written internally. This is the same class of conservative warning previously recorded in repair_memory and explicitly overridden by SL-10: the NL says the FSM reads demand, renewable contributions, SoC, and capacity bounds to select dispatch states, and it does not define internal update equations for those external inputs or capacity parameters. Adding writes solely to silence these warnings would invent plant/environment dynamics and violate the forbidden edits.

The new guard-never-change instances are attached to InitialDispatchSelect only because the repair correctly uses the same NL-grounded classification predicates during initial routing that were already used by the dynamic forced transitions. Simplifying or deleting those guards would either fail the hard zero-load initial scenario again or weaken the required twelve-state dispatch classification. Therefore the local design diagnostic is not a valid reason to reject this candidate under the NL and FixLog context.

Local SD-10 also reports forced_transition_count_drift old=144 new=156 with fix_target=sim and drift_risk=major. The count increase is an expected and bounded structural consequence of adding one pseudo selector with twelve outgoing guarded classification transitions so that default initialization can enter the same dispatch state that the existing forced transitions would select after initialization. It does not add a new dispatch behavior, delete required behavior, or alter state actions; it duplicates the existing classification formulas only for initial selection.

The FixLog repair_memory instructed not to keep reworking previously overridden local-only external-input warnings unless new hard evidence or real regression appears. Here the new hard evidence was a simulation failure caused by the old fixed initial transition, and SL-9 repaired that exact failure without changing the previously accepted guard-driven dispatch frontier. Local evidence reports regression_detected=false, and the scenario repair brief’s expected state/vars are now matched by the candidate’s InitialDispatchSelect -> ZeroLoadCharge route plus the preserved ZeroLoadCharge enter action.

Although the local checker labels drift_risk as major due to transition-count drift, the NL plus FixLog justify an audited override: the pseudo selector is a narrow initialization mechanism, all twelve NL-required finite states and actions remain intact, no artificial input updates are introduced, and the only behavioral change is to make the first default-init classification obey the same zero-load and dispatch guards already required for dynamic operation.

local_override_rationale: Local SD-10 reports target_resolved=false with reason new_blocking_design_diagnostic because the new InitialDispatchSelect outgoing guards read PL, Ppv, Pw, SoC, battery_Pmax, Plngmax, Pgmax, Pd1max, Pd2max, and eng3_Pmax, which are not written internally. This is the same class of conservative warning previously recorded in repair_memory and explicitly overridden by SL-10: the NL says the FSM reads demand, renewable contributions, SoC, and capacity bounds to select dispatch states, and it does not define internal update equations for those external inputs or capacity parameters. Adding writes solely to silence these warnings would invent plant/environment dynamics and violate the forbidden edits.

The new guard-never-change instances are attached to InitialDispatchSelect only because the repair correctly uses the same NL-grounded classification predicates during initial routing that were already used by the dynamic forced transitions. Simplifying or deleting those guards would either fail the hard zero-load initial scenario again or weaken the required twelve-state dispatch classification. Therefore the local design diagnostic is not a valid reason to reject this candidate under the NL and FixLog context.

Local SD-10 also reports forced_transition_count_drift old=144 new=156 with fix_target=sim and drift_risk=major. The count increase is an expected and bounded structural consequence of adding one pseudo selector with twelve outgoing guarded classification transitions so that default initialization can enter the same dispatch state that the existing forced transitions would select after initialization. It does not add a new dispatch behavior, delete required behavior, or alter state actions; it duplicates the existing classification formulas only for initial selection.

The FixLog repair_memory instructed not to keep reworking previously overridden local-only external-input warnings unless new hard evidence or real regression appears. Here the new hard evidence was a simulation failure caused by the old fixed initial transition, and SL-9 repaired that exact failure without changing the previously accepted guard-driven dispatch frontier. Local evidence reports regression_detected=false, and the scenario repair brief’s expected state/vars are now matched by the candidate’s InitialDispatchSelect -> ZeroLoadCharge route plus the preserved ZeroLoadCharge enter action.

Although the local checker labels drift_risk as major due to transition-count drift, the NL plus FixLog justify an audited override: the pseudo selector is a narrow initialization mechanism, all twelve NL-required finite states and actions remain intact, no artificial input updates are introduced, and the only behavioral change is to make the first default-init classification obey the same zero-load and dispatch guards already required for dynamic operation.

The actual state was LNGShipEMS.RESCoversCharge because the root initial transition was hardwired to RESCoversCharge before the guard-driven forced transitions could select the zero-load branch. The smallest safe repair is to route the initial transition through a pseudo dispatch selector with the same NL-grounded guard conditions as the dynamic forced transitions, so default initialization selects ZeroLoadCharge for PL==0 and preserves the existing twelve dispatch states and subsequent dynamic guard behavior.

The prior waived local objections about external inputs and capacity bounds remain audit-only; no dummy writes or ungrounded plant dynamics were added.

decisions.rationale: The BatteryAssist guard reads PL, Ppv, Pw, SoC, and battery_Pmax, which are NL-grounded external/time-varying inputs or capacity bounds. The FixLog already waived this warning class, and the current batch provides no new hard evidence requiring invented internal writes or guard simplification.

The LNGDispatch guard is an NL-required dispatch classifier over external demand, renewable inputs, SoC, battery capacity, and LNG capacity. Adding writes would invent plant dynamics; simplifying the guard would weaken required dispatch logic. This repeats the previously waived external-input warning class.
The LNGChargeMargin guard preserves the NL-required low-SoC Pgmax/5 charging-margin branch. Its variables are external inputs or capacity bounds, so no meaningful DSL write is grounded in the NL.
The LNGDG3Dispatch guard uses residual demand and eng3_Pmax/LNG capacity bounds exactly as required by the NL. This is a guard-driven input-classification FSM; no internal update rule is provided.
The LNGDG3ChargeMargin guard preserves the NL-required low-SoC Pd1max/10 charging-margin branch. The guard variables are external inputs/capacity bounds and should not be dummy-written.
The AddDG1LastPriority guard implements the required DG1 last-priority branch over demand, renewable generation, and capacity bounds. No new evidence justifies changing or weakening it.
The AddDG2LastPriority guard implements the required DG2 last-priority branch. Its variables are external inputs/capacity bounds; adding writes or simplifying the predicate would reduce NL fidelity.

The ExtremeOverloadBatteryLack guard is required by the overload requirement and depends on external demand, renewable inputs, and thermal capacity bounds. This warning class was previously waived and remains audit-only.

All twelve required finite dispatch states, output assignments, cut-in/cut-out commands, low-SoC margins Pgmax/5 and Pd1max/10, and the extreme overload battery-lack branch are preserved.

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start: with positive load covered by RES and SoC exactly 0.95, residual renewable power should be reported as spare.
scenario_results.name: res_covers_spare_at_soc_threshold

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start: when RES is short, SoC is suitable, and the deficit exactly equals battery_Pmax, batteries should cover the deficit before LNG or diesels.
scenario_results.name: battery_assist_at_battery_capacity_boundary

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start: when battery alone is insufficient and the deficit exactly equals LNG capacity, LNG should be cut in before diesel units.
scenario_results.name: lng_dispatch_at_lng_capacity_boundary

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start: at low SoC exactly 0.20, the LNG-covered branch should add the Pgmax/5 charging margin.
scenario_results.name: lng_charge_margin_low_soc_boundary

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start: when LNG alone is insufficient and the deficit exactly fits LNG plus DG3 capacity, LNG and DG3 should be used before DG1/DG2.
scenario_results.name: lng_dg3_dispatch_at_eng3_boundary

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start: in a later low-SoC diesel-generator case, the Pd1max/10 charging margin should be added while using LNG and DG3.
scenario_results.name: lng_dg3_charge_margin_pd1_margin

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start: when the deficit exceeds LNG plus DG3 but exactly fits after adding DG1, DG1 is cut in and DG2 remains cut out.
scenario_results.name: add_dg1_last_priority_boundary

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start: when the deficit exceeds LNG plus DG3 plus DG1 but exactly fits after adding DG2, both DG1 and DG2 are cut in as last-priority units.
scenario_results.name: add_dg2_last_priority_boundary

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start: for demand exceeding all RES and thermal resources, all thermal units are activated and the remaining lack is covered by battery discharge in the illegal overload state.
scenario_results.name: extreme_overload_all_thermal_and_battery_lack

evidence: NL states: "batteries when SoC is suitable" and "Low-SoC branches" but does not explicitly define SoC > 0.20 or SoC <= 0.20.
DSL guards use SoC > 0.20 for BatteryAssist/LNGDispatch/LNGDG3Dispatch and SoC <= 0.20 for LNGChargeMargin/LNGDG3ChargeMargin.
GroundingMap.source_summary assumption says exact original branch formulas are not all provided and the model names states from described cases.
findings.summary: The model is broadly faithful, but some transition thresholds and formulas are inferred rather than explicitly present in the NL, especially the fixed SoC low threshold of 0.20 and several capacity-bound choices beyond the explicitly named eng3_Pmax, Pgmax/5, and Pd1max/10.

evidence: DSL LNGChargeMargin guard requires SoC <= 0.20 and PL - Ppv - Pw + Pgmax / 5 <= Plngmax.
DSL LNGDG3ChargeMargin guard requires SoC <= 0.20 and PL - Ppv - Pw + Pd1max / 10 > Plngmax and <= Plngmax + eng3_Pmax.
There is no explicit default/error/diagnostic state for positive-load RES-short cases not satisfying any of the twelve forced guards.
NL says twelve states are selected by logical conditions over demand, generation, capacity, and SoC, implying complete dispatch classification as resources and demand vary.
findings.summary: Some low-SoC operating regions appear under-specified or potentially uncovered by the explicit charge-margin guards. In particular, low-SoC deficits that cannot fit the LNG Pgmax/5 margin but also do not satisfy the later Pd1max/10 DG3 margin may fall through to no modeled dispatch state, depending on capacities.

findings.summary: The model is a guard-driven condition-classification machine using root-level forced transitions from every state to every state; this is acceptable as an abstraction here but leaves state modes largely decorative and produces many guard-variable-never-change diagnostics.

evidence: NL states: "The overload completion state is illegal... EMS activates all thermal generating units, covers the lack by battery discharge, and the state shall never occur in practice."
DSL ExtremeOverloadBatteryLack sets cut_in_LNG = 1, cut_in_DG1 = 1, cut_in_DG2 = 1, cut_in_DG3 = 1.
DSL ExtremeOverloadBatteryLack sets battery_discharge_power to the remaining lack and illegal_overload = 1.
GroundingMap marks ExtremeOverloadBatteryLack and OverloadOutputs as required with confidence 0.9.
findings.summary: The reachable illegal overload branch is not treated as a blocking unsafe recovery issue because it explicitly marks the violation and implements the NL-described fail-safe/diagnostic behavior rather than silently normalizing the condition.
